title: Lifecycle event (v2)
description: A distinct event/v2 corpus object. First-party contract publish events carry an immutable digest profile and durable publication identity; event/v1 remains unchanged for historical replay and ordinary lifecycle writers.

activation.description: P5's AC1 discharge (docs/features/active/agent-exchange-2026-08/specs/05-declared-nature.md, 2026-08-10 amendment, importing docs/inbox/agent-exchange-review/04-design-agent-seat.md's Metadata table verbatim): the act that moves a contract's `x_operational[]` items (envelope/v2/contract.schema.json) toward `ready` -- an EVENT, not a descriptor field, because a descriptor is immutable after publication and readiness changes after publication without the interface itself changing. Keyed PER VERSION (`version` below), distinct from `consumes.yaml`'s per-major registration -- readiness is a property of a published version, registration a standing relationship to a major. Conditionally required on `activate` below.

version.description: The published contract version this activation covers.

satisfies.description: Which `x_operational[]` item names this activation makes ready. Free text, matching x_operational[].name -- not a closed enum here either.

verdicts.description: P6 wave C (docs/features/active/agent-exchange-2026-08/specs/06-incompleteness.md §7/§11, threat-model.md T5, readiness audit row 25): the verifier's own mirror of a response's `unmet[]` (envelope/v2/response.schema.json) — one entry per judged criterion, indexed into the SAME parent `acceptance_criteria[]` by the same grammar (never restated in prose), so a false verdict has a named author (`cause_owner`) rather than living only in a transition-free note. Conditionally required on `verify`/`close` below. Index-range validation against the parent is internal/validate's job (REF-019), not this schema's — mirroring how `unmet[]`'s own range check (REF-018) lives off envelope/v2/response.schema.json too.

index.description: Index into the parent's acceptance_criteria[] this verdict judges — the same by-index grammar unmet[] uses, checked for range by REF-019.

cause_owner.description: Who the verifier holds responsible for a non-met verdict — the attributability T5 names as its only discharge. Present on every entry, including `met` ones, so the array cannot mix attributed and unattributed judgements.

then.description: T5's discharge: a verify or close over a parent's acceptance criteria must name a per-criterion verdict, not leave the judgement in prose. No minItems floor — a close over a parent that declares no acceptance_criteria[] at all must stay expressible with an empty array.
P5's AC1 discharge: an `activate` transition against a contract subject must name its own `activation` block — modelled on the `publish` conditional above.
